source: human-verified pending: drafted by Claude from DVNA's published docs and the code, to be reviewed by the owner

flaws.title: User search joins the login into a raw SQL string
flaws.why: userSearch builds "SELECT name,id FROM Users WHERE login='" + req.body.login + "'" and runs it with db.sequelize.query, so a UNION can read any column of any table, including password hashes.

flaws.title: Ping passes the address to a shell
flaws.why: exec('ping -c 2 ' + req.body.address, ...) runs through /bin/sh, so input like 'x; id' runs any command on the server.

flaws.title: Calculator evaluates user input with mathjs.eval
flaws.why: calc passes req.body.eqn straight to mathjs.eval; with mathjs 3.10.1 an expression such as cos.constructor(...) escapes the sandbox and runs JavaScript on the server.

flaws.title: Password reset token is md5 of the login name
flaws.why: resetPw and resetPwSubmit accept any request where req.query.token / req.body.token == md5(login), so anyone can compute the token and reset any user's password; there is no stored, random or expiring token.

flaws.title: Hard-coded, well-known session secret
flaws.why: The session is signed with secret: 'keyboard cat', the value from the express-session examples, so session cookies can be forged.

flaws.title: Session cookie sent over plain HTTP, no SameSite
flaws.why: cookie: { secure: false } with no sameSite lets the session cookie travel over HTTP and on cross-site requests.

flaws.title: Session id not renewed at login
flaws.why: Login uses passport.authenticate('login') with passport 0.4 and saveUninitialized: true, which keeps the pre-login session id, so a fixed session id stays valid after the victim logs in.

flaws.title: No limit on failed login attempts
flaws.why: The 'login' LocalStrategy checks bCrypt.compareSync and returns 'Invalid Credentials' with no lockout, delay or rate limit, so passwords can be brute-forced.

flaws.title: Password change does not ask for the current password
flaws.why: userEditSubmit sets user.password from req.body.password when it equals req.body.cpassword, with no check of the old password, so a stolen session or CSRF can take over the account.

flaws.title: No password strength rule at sign-up or reset
flaws.why: The 'signup' strategy only checks that the fields are present and that cpassword == password; any one-character password is accepted.

flaws.title: Forgot and reset password tell whether a login exists
flaws.why: forgotPw answers 'Check email for reset link' for a known login and 'Invalid login username' otherwise (resetPw does the same at lines 58-60), so logins can be enumerated.

flaws.title: Users API returns full user rows, password hashes included
flaws.why: listUsersAPI sends db.User.findAll({}) as JSON with no attributes filter, so every user's bcrypt password hash, login and role reach the browser.

flaws.title: Sequelize logs every SQL query to the console
flaws.why: new Sequelize(...) is created without logging: false, so every query, including password hashes being written and user input, goes to stdout logs.

flaws.title: XML bulk import expands external entities
flaws.why: bulkProducts calls libxmljs.parseXmlString(..., {noent:true, ...}), which substitutes SYSTEM entities, so an upload can read local files such as /etc/passwd into a product description.

flaws.title: Admin users API has no admin check
flaws.why: /admin/usersapi and /admin/users are guarded only by authHandler.isAuthenticated; the role check req.user.role == 'admin' is used only to toggle the dashboard view, so any logged-in user can list all users.

flaws.title: Admin dashboard hides admin links only in client-side script
flaws.why: The 'List Users' link is always in the HTML and is only hidden by var isAdmin = <%=admin%> and style.display = 'none', so the admin URLs are visible in page source.

flaws.title: Edit user trusts the id in the form (IDOR, account takeover)
flaws.why: userEditSubmit loads the user with where: { 'id': req.body.id } instead of req.user.id, so any logged-in user can change any other user's password, email and name.

flaws.title: Any logged-in user can create, change and bulk-import products
flaws.why: POST /modifyproduct, /bulkproducts and /bulkproductslegacy need only authHandler.isAuthenticated; there is no role or ownership check on catalogue writes.

flaws.title: Learn page builds an include path from the URL parameter
flaws.why: vuln_scenario: req.params.vuln + '/scenario' is passed to <%- include(vuln_scenario) %> in views/vulnerabilities/layout.ejs, so an encoded ../ can render other server-side .ejs files named scenario/description/reference.

flaws.title: Calculator errors return a stack trace
flaws.why: mathjs.eval(req.body.eqn) has no try/catch, so invalid input such as 'XD' throws to Express's default handler, which in development mode sends the stack trace with file paths.

flaws.title: X-Powered-By and other security headers left at defaults
flaws.why: The app never calls app.disable('x-powered-by') and never wires the x-xss-protection package from package.json (or any CSP/frame headers), so responses advertise Express and carry no protective headers.

flaws.title: Product save errors are shown to the user
flaws.why: modifyProductSubmit's catch does req.flash('danger', err), sending the raw Sequelize/MySQL error (constraint names, SQL details) to the page.

flaws.title: Docker image copies the env file with database credentials and runs as root
flaws.why: COPY . . with a .dockerignore that lists only node_modules and npm-debug.log bakes vars.env (MySQL credentials, used by docker-compose.yml) into the image; there is no USER line and the base is the end-of-life node:carbon.

flaws.title: Reflected XSS in the product search term
flaws.why: The search term is written with the unescaped tag <%- output.searchTerm %>, and productSearch passes req.body.name into it unchanged.

flaws.title: Stored XSS in the product list
flaws.why: Product id, name, code, tags and description are rendered with <%- ... %>, so script saved through modifyproduct or bulk import runs for every viewer of /app/products.

flaws.title: DOM XSS in the admin user list
flaws.why: appendUsers writes users[i].name and users[i].email from /app/admin/usersapi with innerHTML, so a name like set at sign-up runs in every viewer's browser.

flaws.title: Legacy bulk import deserializes uploads with node-serialize
flaws.why: bulkProductsLegacy calls serialize.unserialize on the uploaded file; a _$$ND_FUNC$$_ value with a trailing () is executed, giving remote code execution.

flaws.title: mathjs pinned to 3.10.1, which has a known sandbox escape
flaws.why: "mathjs": "3.10.1" is an exact pin to a version with a published remote code execution in eval (fixed in later 3.x), which the calculator exposes.

flaws.title: node-serialize 0.0.4 has a known RCE with no fixed version
flaws.why: "node-serialize": "0.0.4" is affected by CVE-2017-5941 (code execution in unserialize) and has no patched release; it should not be a dependency at all.

flaws.title: Other server dependencies resolve to versions with published advisories
flaws.why: The ranges ejs ^2.5.7, express-fileupload ^0.4.0, libxmljs ^0.19.1, mysql2 ^1.4.2, sequelize ^4.13.10 and bcrypt ^1.0.3 stay on old major lines that later received security advisories fixed only in newer majors; there is no lockfile (package-lock.json is git-ignored).

flaws.title: Old front-end libraries loaded from CDNs without integrity checks
flaws.why: Every page loads jquery-3.2.1, bootstrap 3.3.7 and bootstrapValidator 0.5.3 (versions with known XSS advisories) from third-party CDNs with no integrity attribute, and html5shim over plain http.

flaws.title: Security events are not logged
flaws.why: Failed and successful logins, password resets and user edits write no log entry; the only logging is morgan('tiny') access lines in server.js, and the winston dependency is never used.

flaws.title: No CSRF protection on state-changing forms
flaws.why: No POST route uses a CSRF token (csurf is in package.json but never required), so a cross-site form can add products or, with useredit, change the victim's password; ping and calc POSTs make it a path to RCE.

flaws.title: Open redirect, reachable without login
flaws.why: redirect does res.redirect(req.query.url) with no allow-list, and routes/app.js line 48 mounts /app/redirect without isAuthenticated, so the site's domain can front phishing links.

flaws.title: Forgot password never sends a reset link
flaws.why: forgotPw only has the comment '// Send reset link via email happens here' and tells the user to check their email, so a real user who forgot the password has no way back in.

flaws.title: Sign-up duplicate check compares the wrong column and hangs on conflict
flaws.why: findOrCreateUser looks up where: { 'email': username } (the login, not the email), so a taken login reaches db.User.create, fails the unique constraint, and with no .catch the request never gets a response.

flaws.title: Edit user crashes on an unknown id or missing password field
flaws.why: userEditSubmit reads req.body.password.length and user.password with no null checks and no .catch on the promise chain, so a missing user or field throws and the request hangs.

flaws.title: Duplicated password check makes the 'Invalid Password' branch dead code
flaws.why: The inner if(req.body.password.length>0) repeats the outer one, so the else branch that flashes 'Invalid Password' can never run.

flaws.title: Bulk imports ignore save failures and crash on bad input
flaws.why: Both bulk handlers call newProduct.save() without waiting or catching and redirect at once, so rows that fail (duplicate code, missing name) vanish silently; req.files.products throws when no file is sent, and malformed XML or a non-array JSON throws to the default error page.

flaws.title: Database promise chains have no error handling
flaws.why: listProducts, productSearch and modifyProduct (and forgotPw/resetPw in core/authHandler.js) use .then with no .catch, so a database error leaves the request hanging with an unhandled rejection.

flaws.title: Product and user lists load every row with no paging
flaws.why: listProducts calls db.Product.findAll() and listUsersAPI (lines 206-213) calls db.User.findAll({}) with no limit or offset, so the pages grow without bound with the data.

flaws.title: Handlers assign to an undeclared global 'output'
flaws.why: ping (and listProducts, productSearch, modifyProduct, modifyProductSubmit) write output = ... without var/let, creating a module-wide global shared by all requests instead of a local.

flaws.title: Reset form loses login and token after a password mismatch
flaws.why: On a mismatch resetPwSubmit re-renders resetpw with req.query.login and req.query.token, which are empty on this POST, so the user cannot retry from the form.

flaws.title: Admin user table loop reads one past the end
flaws.why: while(i<=users.length) runs once more than there are users, so users[i].id throws a TypeError after the last row is added.
